title: feat(app-shell): a console list's Filter-panel conditions, search term and sort live in the URL (objectui#11860)
body:
Part of #11860

Clause-②: no

The first line is `Part of` on purpose: this PR delivers the Filter panel's conditions, the search term and the sort. Toolbar grouping is the card's fourth piece and is NOT here (see "Grouping: stopped" below), so merging this must leave the card open.

## What changes

A console object list (`/apps/APP/OBJECT` and `/apps/APP/OBJECT/view/VIEW`) now writes three more pieces of its toolbar state into the URL and restores them on load, so a filtered, searched and sorted list can be shared as a link or bookmarked:

| Param | Carries | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `uf__filter` | the Filter panel's conditions | JSON `{ logic, conditions }`, each condition one spec `ViewFilterRule` (`{ field, operator, value }`) |
| `uf__search` | the search term | the term |
| `uf__sort` | the sort | JSON, the spec `ListViewSchema.sort` array (`[{ field, order }]`); a cleared sort is `[]` |

These extend the `uf_` family that ADR-0047's quick-filter persistence already uses (`uf_FIELD`, `uf__tab`), as three more reserved underscore keys. `userFilterUrlState.ts` owns the whole family. `parseUserFilterParams` keeps the new keys out of the quick-filter selections it hands to `UserFilters`.

Files: `userFilterUrlState.ts` (the URL read and write), `ObjectView.tsx` (seed on load, write on change), two new test files, and `.changeset/11860-list-url-state.md` (app-shell patch). `ListView.tsx` is not touched, so there is no overlap with objectui#11896.

## Precedence on load

The claim asks for this to be stated.

1. **The URL carries `uf_*` state this page did not write itself** (an opened link, a reload, Back). The URL is then the whole state. The per-browser cache (`listFilterStorage`) is not consulted, so a shared link opens the same list for every user who may read it. A piece the URL does not carry starts empty; it is not filled from the cache.
2. **Otherwise**, the cache restores the Filter panel and the search term, as before. The sort is the view's own (the cache holds no sort).
3. **Then the seed is written back into the URL** with `replace`. The address bar now shows a filter restored from the cache, and an entry dropped on load is removed from it.

`listFilterStorage.ts` is not edited. The cache is still written on every change and still read when the URL carries nothing. Opening a link does not overwrite it.

"Did this page write it" is tracked in `ownListParamsRef`. When the active view changes without a navigation (saved views arrive after the first render, and the user's default becomes active), params this page wrote for the first view are not read as a link to the second. A link's own params are never marked as this page's writes, so a link still applies to the view it names when that view resolves late. Both directions are pinned.

## History, view switching, panels

- Every write uses `replace`. Typing a search term adds no history entries, and one Back leaves the list (pinned).
- A view switch navigates to a path with no query string, so the next view opens from its own cache. The previous view's params do not follow it, and Back restores the first view as it was (pinned).
- Panels and dialogs stay out of the URL. Opening and closing the Filter panel and the search box leaves the URL unchanged (pinned, as the triage control asked).

## Mechanism hypotheses, measured

**H1 (where each piece lives, and whether `ListView` already reports and accepts it):**

| Piece | State in `ListView` | Reports to host | Accepts initial value | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Filter panel | `currentFilters` | `onFilterChange` | `initialFilters` | host-side |
| Search term | `searchInput` | `onSearchChange` | `initialSearchTerm` | host-side |
| Sort | `currentSort` | `onSortChange` (the host already persists it to the view row) | `schema.sort`, which the host builds | host-side |
| Grouping | `groupingConfig` | **none** | `schema.grouping` | **stop** |

The sort has one consequence. `ListView` reads `schema.sort` as the list's declared sort, so when a URL carries a sort, "reset to default" returns to that sort. A sort the host has stored behaves the same way today.

**H2 (encoding):** the filter AST in `@objectstack/spec/data` was measured and rejected for the Filter panel. It is the query format, and a round trip through it loses the row the user built: `before` comes back as `less_than`, and an `in` row comes back as an OR of equalities. The spec's own list-view filter rule (`ViewFilterRule`, the shape `ListViewSchema.filter` stores) carries each row losslessly, because the builder's operator ids are its enum since objectui#9306. Rows are written through `foldFilterGroupToSpecRules`, the function "save as view" uses: blank and unfinished rows are not written, row ids are stripped, and operators are canonical. That rule list can only express AND, but the panel offers OR, so the group's `logic` travels beside the rows. Reads go through `ViewFilterRuleSchema` and the element schema of `ListViewSchema.sort`. A value that is not JSON, a rule or sort entry the spec rejects, and a field the object does not declare or (once permissions have loaded) the user cannot read are each dropped. The list still opens and nothing throws. The round trip and the malformed cases are pinned.

**H3:** precedence is stated above. Replace-not-push, the clean view switch, and late view resolution are measured and pinned. For a user the server refuses, the page shows the same `forbidden` panel, with the same text, with or without list state in the URL. The query still carried the link's filter, so the refusal is the server's answer to the same request shape.

## Grouping: stopped

Writing grouping to the URL needs a change notification that `ListView` does not have. The grouping editor in the toolbar and the one in the compact View-settings popover both call `setGroupingConfig` directly, and `ListViewProps` has no grouping callback. Adding one would widen a published `@object-ui/plugin-list` prop, which the claim names as a stop, so it is not added. Seeding grouping from the URL alone (through `schema.grouping`) is not landed either: the next grouping change could not update the param, and the URL would show stale grouping. The seat re-claims with `Clause-②: yes` for this half.

## Tests

- `userFilterUrlState.listState-11860.test.ts` (16 tests): the round trip of each piece through a real query string (AND and OR groups; `equals`, `before`, `in`, `between`, `is_empty`); spec-shaped values (no row id, canonical operators, each one a valid `ViewFilterRule`); unfinished rows not written; malformed and stale values dropped; a cleared sort kept as `[]`; reserved keys kept out of `parseUserFilterParams`.
- `ObjectView.listUrlState-11860.test.tsx` (13 tests): renders this page, `plugin-view`'s `ObjectView` and `plugin-list`'s `ListView` for real, and reads the query at the data source.

**Ablations.** Each was committed first, mutated through `ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit 1, blob moved), run, and restored from `HEAD` (blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty). The subject is imported by a relative path, so no `dist` is involved. Each prediction was written down before its run:

| Mutation | Predicted | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| A: the URL never seeds the list | 7 red / 6 green | 7 failed / 6 passed |
| B: no own-write tracking | 1 red (the late-resolving mirrored-params case) | 1 failed / 12 passed |
| C: a search change is not written to the URL | 2 red (replace-history, cleared search) | 2 failed / 11 passed |

## Gates

The gate list was derived by hand from this repo's `package.json` and `.github/workflows/lint.yml`, since `dispatch-gates.mjs` exists only in objectstack. `pnpm lint` and the full `pnpm test` belong to CI and were not run here. `@object-ui/plugin-list` is untouched, so its type-check is not owed.

## Acceptance notes

- **No doc changed.** No README or `content/docs` sentence describes a list's URL state today. A grep for `uf_`, the list-filter cache and share-link wording finds none, so the docs-driven rule had nothing to update. A new README paragraph under app-shell's `ObjectView` section would be outside the claim's file list, so it is left to the seat.
- **`listFilterStorage.ts`'s header** still describes the URL family as carrying quick filters only. That sentence is now incomplete. It is a comment, and the file is on the claim's "not on it" list, so it was not edited. Carrier: none.
- **`InterfaceListPage.tsx` and `ObjectDataPage.tsx`** render a `ListView`, but they are other surfaces with their own URL contracts (interface mode, which is ADR-0047's open question 1, and the ADR-0055 `/data` surface). Neither reads `listFilterStorage`. They are not changed, except that `parseUserFilterParams` (which both call) now skips the three reserved keys.
- **Read in source only, not measured:** the quick-filter seed `initialUfSelections` is captured once per page mount from `window.location.search`. A view switch between two `view/VIEW` paths keeps the page mounted, so the next view's `UserFilters` may restore the first view's quick-filter selections while the URL no longer carries them. A probe did not produce a reading. Carrier: none.
- **Read in source only, not measured:** the Filter panel's field list (`filterFields` in `ListView`) does not check field-level read permission, while the list's columns do. The URL read added here does check it once permissions have loaded. Whether the server enforces field-level permission on a filter was not measured. Carrier: none.
